unit.why: A short anecdote quoted from the preface of Zohar Hai: R. Zvi of Zhidachov blesses his six-year-old son to lose his ruach ha-kodesh until age thirty, the child agrees, and it departs from him at once.

stories.end_quote: נסתלק ממנו הרוה״ק שהי׳ לו מקודם
stories.summary_en: When his son reached his sixth year, R. Zvi of Zhidachov blessed him to stop speaking with the holy spirit until age thirty so it would not harm his simple Jewish piety; the child agreed and the holy spirit immediately left him.

quotes: מיין קינד איך וועל דיך בענטשין
tags.why: Father-tsaddik and his child are the protagonists

quotes: דוא זאלסט שוין נישט זאגין קיין רוח הקודש
נסתלק ממנו הרוה״ק שהי׳ לו מקודם
tags.why: The child possessed ruach ha-kodesh (supernatural knowledge)
The blessing immediately removes the child's holy spirit, a discrete before/after supernatural event
Worshipping God in simplicity rather than with displays of spiritual gifts

quotes: וכשתהי׳ בן שלשים ותרצה אז אחזור לך המדריגה
tags.why: Promise that the spiritual level will return at thirty
Father acts as spiritual guide shaping the son's path
The anecdote illustrates the tsaddik's preference for simple, unassuming worship

missing_concepts: deliberate renunciation or suspension of spiritual gifts
